criteria.justification: The response clearly commits to immediate containment: disable the new integration’s inclusion path if verified effective, otherwise roll back to the last known-good version.

It frames withdrawal as a “temporary pause” followed by relaunch after a tested fix, contrasting that reversible loss of launch availability with the accumulating harm of leaving the faulty feature live.
It explicitly acknowledges that the public announcement matters for trust but concludes it does not justify continuing mistaken signals for unrelated customers while a permanent fix takes days.
The response conditions the fast mitigation on confirmation that it stops the faulty calibration and calls for broader rollback if it cannot be verified or fails to stop impact.
It specifies post-containment monitoring, impact identification, support guidance, customer communication, a factual availability update, and relaunch only after the fix is tested.
